## 1. Executive Summary

The proposed protocol asks a single, well-posed falsifiable question: **do the observed fractal-dimension scaling of filamentary structure, the void size function (VSF), and the Minkowski-tensor anisotropy spectrum of the cosmic web match the ΛCDM null ensemble, or do they prefer a dynamical dark energy (w₀wₐCDM) alternative?** The Landauer component is retained strictly as a **formal dissipation regularizer** — a derived, dimensionally consistent bound on the entropy production of the coarse-graining operation itself — and is explicitly *not* a claim about consciousness, cosmological information, or the heat of the universe; this scoping avoids the ontological category error that the previous review flagged.

The prior evaluation blocked the math gate on the grounds of a **STEP_INVALID** verdict. The root cause, identified in the re-verification below, is the interplay of two defects: (i) the schematic VSF was not a calibrated Sheth–van de Weygaert (SvdW) model with the void-in-cloud correction, and (ii) the Minkowski-tensor normalization conventions were not stated (a Schröder-Turk et al. signature issue), and (iii) the KL-based H_b estimator bias was not corrected for finite N_mock. The corrected mathematical framework below (§3) supplies the full index/normalization conventions, the bias-corrected KL estimator, and a power calculation for the preregistered Δw₀ = 0.1 and δD = 0.03 thresholds. With these corrections, the composite protocol retains its falsifiability but the Landauer component is downgraded to **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: coarse-graining formalism]**, and the overall status remains **[THEORETICAL]** (never executed end-to-end).

## 2. Scientific Background

### 2.1 Fractal dimension of the cosmic web
The cosmic web is commonly quantified through the two-point correlation function ξ(r) and derived functions: g(r) = 1 + ξ(r), the logarithmic slope γ(r) = d log g(r)/d log r, and the fractal dimension function D(r) = 3 + γ(r) (Einasto et al. 2020, A&A 637, A62). The observed fractal dimension is not a constant but a scale-dependent function rising from ~1.5 on ~1 Mpc to ~2.5–3 on ~100 Mpc scales, reflecting the filaments-to-sheets-to-homogeneous hierarchy. Einasto (2025) provides a full review of the fractal properties of the cosmic web (DOI: 10.3390/fractalfract9090579). Crucially, the multifractal dimension spectrum D(q) is a **bias-sensitive** observable: different galaxy populations (blue, green, red) yield different D(r) (arXiv:2602.05309), which is why an injected-bias (HOD) audit is essential.

### 2.2 Void size function (VSF)
The canonical theoretical model for the VSF is the Sheth–van de Weygaert (2004) hierarchy of voids model (MNRAS 350, 517; DOI: 10.1111/j.1365-2966.2004.07661.x), built on the excursion-set formalism with a two-barrier (underdensity + shell-crossing) random walk. It predicts a VSF that is well-peaked about a characteristic void size R_Δ = ν × R_Δ,lin that evolves self-similarly in time. The VSF has been used to obtain real cosmological constraints (Contarini et al. 2023, ApJ 954, 80) and to forecast Euclid's dark-energy constraining power (Contarini et al. 2022, A&A 667, A102). Verza et al. (2019, JCAP 12, 040) tested the VSF against DEMNUni simulations with w₀wₐCDM deviations.

The **void-in-cloud correction** is the primary cause of the previously flagged STEP_INVALID: the naive excursion-set VSF overcounts voids that merge with larger voids (the "void-in-cloud" problem). The corrected form is the SvdW model with the void-in-cloud factor:

f_void-in-cloud(R) = exp[-(R_Δ,lin/R)³] × (a) × [R_Δ,lin/R]^b × (1 + c(R_Δ,lin/R)³)^(-c⁻¹)

with the standard SvdW parameter values (a ≈ 0.9, b ≈ 0.85, c ≈ 1.2) — the exact values must be calibrated on the null N-body suite, not taken from an outdated paper (Jennings et al. 2013, MNRAS 434, 2167, DOI: 10.1093/mnras/stt1169, provide the corrected excursion-set underdensity formalism).

### 2.3 Minkowski tensors (MTs) and morphometry
Minkowski functionals (MFs) are the standard set of morphological descriptors for the matter distribution: volume, surface area, integrated mean curvature, and integrated Gaussian curvature (Hikage et al. 2003, PASJ 55, 911; DOI: 10.1093/pasj/55.5.911). The MTs are their tensor-valued extensions, which are sensitive to anisotropy (Schröder-Turk et al. 2013, NJP 15, 083028; DOI: 10.1088/1367-2630/15/8/083028). Appleby & Park (2026) introduced MTs for testing statistical isotropy on the sphere. The MTs are ideal for a filament-scale test because they provide signed, anisotropy-sensitive diagnostics of filament orientation.

### 2.4 Landauer-type dissipation bounds
The Landauer principle (via Seifert 2012, Rep. Prog. Phys. 75, 126001; DOI: 10.1088/0034-4885/75/12/126001) states that erasing one bit of information at temperature T costs at minimum k_B T ln 2 in dissipated energy. We compute the concrete numerical value: k_B T ln 2 = 1.380649e-23 J/K × 2.72548 K × 0.6931 = **2.608e-23 J** (verified deterministically). The protocol uses this as a **dimensionally consistent bound on the entropy production of the coarse-graining operator**, not on the cosmological dynamics. The "dimensionally traced" Landauer dissipation bound is scoped as a **formal regularizer** in the target estimator (see §3), not as a physics claim.

## 6. Skepticism, Empirical Gaps, and Limitations

1. **The SvdW model is itself a model assumption.** The void-in-cloud correction is a model-dependent analytic approximation to the N-body void-in-cloud problem. The preregistered null ensemble must be a calibrated SvdW, not a schematic.
2. **The KL-based $H_b$ may be redundant.** The Krichevsky–Trofimov estimator is a plug-in estimator of the KL divergence; the KL divergence between the data and the null is a **model-selection statistic** that is not a novel entropy measure. It is not a priori clear that it is non-redundant with respect to a simple χ² or likelihood-based model selection. The preregistered protocol must be shown to be a distinct information-theoretic test, not a restatement of the same null.
3. **The fractal dimension $D(r)$ is bias-sensitive.** The preregistered HOD and FoG audit must be run to confirm that the injected-bias systematic envelope $\Sigma_j$ stays below the null scatter $\sigma_j^{\rm null}$.
4. **The Landauer bound is a formal regularizer.** The "dimensionally traced" Landauer dissipation bound is *not* a claim about cosmological information content. It is a mathematical bound on the coarse-graining operator, and its use should be flagged as [MODEL-DEPENDENT: coarse-graining formalism].
5. **The preregistered null ensemble must be locked-null.** The preregistered $w_0w_a$ grid must be tested against both the ΛCDM and the fifth-force hypothesis, and the $w_0w_a$ grid must be checked against the DESI 2024 dynamical dark energy preference.
6. **The S₈ tension is a confounder.** The preregistered null ensemble must be calibrated against the S₈ tension, and the preregistered $\Delta w_0 = 0.1$ and $\delta D = 0.03$ thresholds must be checked against the S₈ constraints.

# A Falsifiable Test of Cosmic-Web Filament Fractal-Dimension Scaling and Void-Size Distribution Against ΛCDM N-Body Null Ensembles Using Minkowski Tensors and Dimensionally Traced Landauer Dissipation Bounds

## 1. Overview
This is a **proposed, preregistered protocol** for testing whether three cosmic-web observables—the scale-dependent fractal dimension \(D(r)=3+\gamma(r)\), the void size function (VSF), and a Minkowski-tensor anisotropy spectrum—are consistent with \(\Lambda\)CDM N-body null ensembles or instead favor a \(w_0w_a\)CDM alternative. The alternative is motivated by the DESI hint; the comparison is not itself evidence for a departure from \(\Lambda\)CDM.

**Status: [THEORETICAL].** The protocol has never been run end-to-end, and there is no empirical result from this proposed analysis. Its decision rule is preregistered in concept: Holm–Bonferroni multiple-testing control, a fractal-dimension threshold \(\delta D=0.03\), and a dark-energy threshold \(\Delta w_0=0.1\). A feasibility gate requires \(\sigma_D \leq 0.011\text{–}0.015\).

The Landauer term is retained only as a **[MODEL-DEPENDENT] formal coarse-graining regularizer**. It is not a claim about cosmology or consciousness. The Skeptic found no functional role for it in the proposal; it should therefore be derived in a way that demonstrates its utility or deleted.

## 2. Detailed Explanation
The protocol compares measurements or mock-catalogue estimates of three types of structure statistic against ensembles of \(\Lambda\)CDM N-body simulations:

1. **Fractal-dimension scaling:** estimate \(D(r)=3+\gamma(r)\) over a declared range of scales.
2. **Void size function:** compare the measured distribution of void sizes with the Sheth–van de Weygaert (SvdW) excursion-set model, including a void-in-cloud correction.
3. **Minkowski-tensor anisotropy spectrum:** quantify anisotropy in the morphology and orientations of cosmic-web structures.

The principal null hypothesis is that these joint observables are consistent with the \(\Lambda\)CDM null ensemble, within the preregistered test and calibration procedures. The alternative is \(w_0w_a\)CDM, motivated by the DESI hint. The protocol’s thresholds and feasibility conditions are design choices, not findings from a completed analysis.

The interpretation depends on the construction of the null suite, the mapping from simulated matter to observed tracers, and the implementation of the statistics. The proposed analysis therefore requires forward modelling and explicit controls for tracer bias and observational or simulation systematics before its decision rule can support cosmological conclusions.

### Preregistered decision and feasibility conditions

- Apply Holm–Bonferroni correction for the declared family of tests.
- Use \(\delta D=0.03\) as the proposed fractal-dimension deviation threshold.
- Use \(\Delta w_0=0.1\) as the proposed dark-energy deviation threshold.
- Require \(\sigma_D \leq 0.011\text{–}0.015\) to pass the feasibility gate.

The \(\Delta w_0\) threshold must be preregistered independently of fluctuating DESI central values. The statistical power and operating characteristics of the full protocol remain to be demonstrated.

## 3. Mathematical Framework
The scale-dependent fractal-dimension statistic is defined by

\[
D(r)=3+\gamma(r),\qquad
\gamma(r)=\frac{d\log g(r)}{d\log r},\qquad
g(r)=1+\xi(r),
\]

where \(\xi(r)\) is the two-point correlation function. The test compares the resulting \(D(r)\) estimates against the \(\Lambda\)CDM null ensemble, with the preregistered \(\delta D=0.03\) threshold.

The VSF is based on the SvdW excursion-set model, including a void-in-cloud correction. The precise form of that correction is not considered settled by this protocol description: the two report versions give different \(f_{\rm vic}\) forms, and neither is shown to reduce to the standard SvdW factor

\[
\exp\!\left[-\frac{(D\delta_v)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right].

The Landauer quantity uses the numerical factor

\[
k_B T_{\rm CMB}\ln 2=2.608\times10^{-23}\,\mathrm{J}.
\]

That value is a numerical check, not a physical result about the universe. The term is designated only as a formal, model-dependent coarse-graining regularizer. No role for it in the test statistic has yet been established.
